sections.heading: Lagrange multipliers: setting up the system

questions.q: Set up the Lagrange multiplier equations to optimize $f(x,y)=xy$ subject to $g(x,y)=x+y-10=0$.
questions.answer: $\nabla f=\lambda\nabla g$: $\langle y,x\rangle=\lambda\langle1,1\rangle \Rightarrow y=\lambda,\ x=\lambda \Rightarrow x=y$, together with the constraint $x+y=10$.
From the setup above, $x=y$ and $x+y=10 \Rightarrow x=y=5$. Maximum value: $f(5,5)=25$.
$\nabla f=\lambda\nabla g$: $\langle2x,2y\rangle=\lambda\langle1,1\rangle \Rightarrow x=y$. With $x+y=4$: $x=y=2$. Minimum value: $f(2,2)=8$.

questions.q: Find the point on the line $x+y=6$ closest to the origin, using Lagrange multipliers on $f(x,y)=x^2+y^2$.
questions.answer: $\nabla f=\lambda\nabla g$: $\langle2x,2y\rangle=\lambda\langle1,1\rangle \Rightarrow x=y$. With $x+y=6$: $x=y=3$. Closest point: $(3,3)$, at distance $\sqrt{9+9}=3\sqrt{2}$.
